summary: SDK connector headroom exhaustion causing request stalls and perceived timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports large numbers of streaming requests from their service appear to stall for 2–6s intermittently and then either succeed or time out. Impact: Customer's real-time summarization pipeline sees elevated tail latency and partial response failures (~8% increase in 5xx/timeouts over last 24h), affecting SLAs for their enterprise customers. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod us-east, SDK v1.4.2 (Python), using streaming endpoints with default SDK connection pool and backoff settings. Observed during normal QPS (approx 120 r/s) with occasional load bursts to 350 r/s.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Use customer SDK config (example below) to open 50 concurrent streaming requests for 30s against the tenant endpoint. 2) Observe per-request response times and note pileups when connection handshakes exceed pool headroom. 3) Repeat with SDK max_connections set to 100 and with default (16).

Customer SDK example (Python):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>", max_connections=16, backoff_strategy="expo", max_retries=5)
# spawn 50 concurrent streaming calls to tenant endpoint

Observed behavior: With default max_connections=16 and high concurrency the customer sees requests queuing on the client side for multiple seconds. When the SDK hits the per-tenant connection limit enforced at the gateway, retries are synchronized (exponential backoff without jitter) and cause head-of-line blocking. When connections are available again the queued requests complete in short bursts which looks like intermittent latency spikes.

Logs/metrics (excerpts):
- customer-side SDK logs: "ConnectionPool exhausted (max_connections=16) - queuing request" repeated at high rate.
- gateway logs: 429s spike correlating to connection limit exceeded for tenant_id=ftm-42 between 2026-03-09T09:12:21Z and 2026-03-09T09:15:03Z.
- serving-runtime: no JVM OOM, CPU stable; per-GPU concurrency reached rollout thresholds during bursts.
- Observed metric: inflight_queue_depth (sdk) rising to ~320 while active connections stayed near 16.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy SDK v1.4.2 with default connection pool (max_connections=16)
Simulate 50+ concurrent streaming requests from a single host against the dedicated tenant endpoint
Monitor client-side ConnectionPool exhausted logs and gateway 429 events
Change max_connections to 100 and observe queue depth change
logs: [2026-03-09T09:12:21Z] SDK INFO ConnectionPool exhausted (max_connections=16) - queuing request id=5f3a
[2026-03-09T09:13:05Z] SDK ERROR request id=5f3a timeout after 6000ms

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Combination of low per-tenant connection quota (16) + SDK default max_connections=16 + exponential backoff with no jitter produced synchronized retries and client-side queueing. This is amplified when ephemeral connector threads exhaust file descriptors and keepalive isn't reusing connections effectively. Evidence: gateway 429s aligned with client queueing spikes; inflight_queue_depth metric tallied against active connections. We measured that enabling jitter and increasing SDK pool to 32 reduced queuing in a controlled test. Also observed keepalive_disabled on some customer hosts leading to higher TCP churn. No evidence of serving-runtime CPU/GPU saturation outside normal burst autoscale windows.
root_cause: Per-tenant connection cap (legacy override) too low for customer's burst profile combined with SDK defaults that do not enable jitter for retries and have conservative max_connections, causing synchronized retry storms and head-of-line blocking on the client side.
workaround: 1) Customer temporary mitigation: set SDK max_connections=32, enable backoff_jitter=true, reduce max_retries to 3. 2) If using many hosts, spread connections across hosts to avoid single-host headroom exhaustion. 3) Request temporary per-tenant headroom bump from platform ops.
resolution: Applied temporary gateway headroom bump for tenant ftm-42 (2026-03-12 02:15 UTC) and pushed SDK guidance to customer. Customer observed tail-latency improvement from ~2–6s spikes down to 200–400ms. Engineering created PR to add jitter by default in next SDK minor (target v1.5.0) and documentation callout for per-tenant caps. Follow-up: scheduled a permanent increase of tenant connection cap after capacity plan review.
follow_up_actions: Add SDK default jitter to backoff policy (PR merged, release scheduled v1.5.0)
Update Support runbook: troubleshooting steps for ConnectionPool exhausted and recommended SDK settings
Capacity review: evaluate per-tenant connection cap policy and auto-bump criteria
Add alerting in Console for per-tenant connection headroom < 20%
notes_for_customer: Thank you for raising this. Short-term please update SDK config as advised (max_connections=32, backoff_jitter=true, max_retries=3). We have temporarily increased your tenant headroom and will follow up with a capacity assurance plan. Expect a final confirmation after the capacity review (target 2026-03-20).
